answer_text:
The recurrence has characteristic equation

\[
r^2-3xr-(1-x-2x^2)=0
=(r-(2x-1))(r-(x+1)).
\]

Thus the sequence has the form

\[
f_n(x)=A(x)(2x-1)^n+B(x)(x+1)^n.
\]

Using \(f_0=2\) and \(f_1=3x\), we get \(A=B=1\), so

\[
f_n(x)=(2x-1)^n+(x+1)^n.
\]

We want divisibility by

\[
x^3-x^2+x=x(x^2-x+1).
\]

Check the roots.

At \(x=0\),

\[
f_n(0)=(-1)^n+1,
\]

so we need \(n\) odd.

Let \(\alpha\) be a root of \(x^2-x+1=0\). Then \(\alpha^3=-1\) and \(\alpha\) has order \(6\). Also,

\[
2\alpha-1=\alpha(\alpha+1).
\]

Therefore,

\[
f_n(\alpha)=(2\alpha-1)^n+(\alpha+1)^n
=(\alpha+1)^n(\alpha^n+1).
\]

Since \(\alpha+1\neq 0\), we need

\[
\alpha^n=-1,
\]

which happens exactly when

\[
n\equiv 3 \pmod 6.
\]

This also implies \(n\) is odd, so all such \(n\) are

\[
n=6k+3,\qquad k\ge 0.
\]

Thus the least positive value is

\[
\boxed{3}.
\]
